title: New frontend to old API: reject success-shaped incompatibility
requiredVisibleLabel: Training rehearsal - synthetic data - not a live Azure result
objective: Send new-frontend requests to old APIs during mixed effective routing; preserve supported old contracts and reject success for unavailable required features.
sourceAcceptance: New clients tolerate supported old contracts; required unsupported features do not silently return success.
preconditions: Standard local browser HTML, CSS and JavaScript; no server or account.
frontend-v2 is loaded before four fixed GET /profile requests.
api-v1/profile.v1 supplies profileId and displayName but not timeZone.
api-v2/profile.v2 supplies the same base contract and timeZone.
Mixed effective routing is old, new, old, new; it is not inferred from desired routing.
actions: Choose effective routing, base/optional/required feature, frontend handling and old-response condition.
Start and manually send each of the four requests.
Inspect response shape, frontend claim and independently checked required-journey outcome.
Check a prediction separately from the actual outcome.
Retain the completed attempt or explicitly reset all defaults and history.
syntheticInput: learning/S052/model.js: fixed profile-synthetic / Aster / Etc/UTC fixture
assertions: Supported old contracts satisfy the new frontend's base profile journey.
Optional absence is visible without inventing timeZone.
Required timeZone absence fails even for HTTP 200 or status-only success claims.
Malformed base contracts and observed timeouts fail; withheld observations remain unknown.
Successful new responses never erase old failures or unknowns.
New-only success explicitly has no old-API compatibility coverage.
All four requests must finish before aggregate success can be established.
Exact input/state guards and eight-attempt retained history prevent silent mutation or pruning.

iac.decisionStage: After genuine loadable-stub assertion RED and before implementation.
iac.reason: Resource-free local synthetic lesson; no infrastructure, cloud or deployment authorized.

limits: Deterministic four-request in-memory compatibility model, not an actual HTTP client/server or routing protocol.
A synthetic compatibility success is not a completed migration, native/platform guarantee or five-nines result.
No credentials, authentication, identity registration, cloud, IaC, scaffold, deployment or spending.
History lasts until explicit reset or page reload; it is never silently pruned.
B-S052 and D-S052 native/source-parent acceptance remain separate and unfulfilled.
One frozen S unit; tests, plumbing and refinement earn no additional units.
Published browser helper's known unattended lifecycle limitation remains; no abandoned prototype is used.
